title: Resistance ratios gave no clear coupling prediction gain in 134 selected Allen mouse electrical pairs
abstract: We tested whether cell input resistance ratios predict electrical pulse coupling asymmetry better than equal coupling in Allen Synaptic Physiology r2.1. The primary sample had 134 mouse VisP pairs in 126 recordings from 114 inferred mice. A fixed passive transfer ratio gave an equal-recording mean gain of 0.0294 squared natural-log units. Its conditional 95 percent donor bootstrap interval was -0.1571 to 0.2125. A donor-held-out calibrated rule also left gain uncertain. A selected subset of 38 pairs with both pulse correlation p-values below 0.05 had a positive gain of 0.1479, but removing small coupling coefficients reversed the primary point gain. This analysis adds relative prediction tests to prior bounded-error screens of the same transfer identity. It is not independent replication. Separate measurement states, fixed summary errors, selection, inferred donors and one region limit the result. No junction rectification or general resistance rule is established. Original code, aggregate evidence, a figure and external retrieval steps support reproduction. External records are not bundled.
